## 2026-05-03 (Sun, evening MT, follow-on) Watchlist.md and Operating_Protocols.md factbases added; W4 PRE-ARCHIVAL MIRRORING step inserted; rule (c) simplified; Claude_Task_Plan.md modified

**Trigger:** Operator-directed "fix as you see fit with best decisions" follow-on to the prior Decision_Log lifecycle/archive policy session, after operator probed gaps via questions about (a) whether Decision_Log grows indefinitely, (b) whether NO-GOs are permanent. Probing surfaced two latent gaps in the prior policy that the open-ended fix instruction authorized addressing.

**Inputs:** Claude_Task_Plan.md post-Part-3 state (737 lines, with FILE CONVENTIONS section + W4 prompt + per-prompt read-access-scope lines added in prior session); /mnt/project/Decision_Log.md latest state (5,600 lines after Part 3 entry); Portfolio_Ledger.md current state (4 open/staged positions); operator-stated framework philosophy "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" + "fresh evaluation always allowed" — used to constrain in-scope vs out-of-scope additions; prior-session search results identifying scattered watchlist/protocol context as the operational gaps.

### Gaps identified (probed by operator via prior turns)

**Gap 1 — Strategy A queue persistence.** Strategy A queue (CAT/LLY/QCOM/AAPL) loses its consolidated representation when session-end consolidation entries archive at 30 days. Individual router-gate NO-GO entries (e.g., AAPL 2026-05-02) also archive at 30 days under rule (d). After ~2026-06-02, "what names are queued for next M1 router ACTIVATE flip?" requires archive reads to reconstruct. M1 has archive read access per the new policy, but would need to actively search archive files for queue-membership references — fragile and easy to miss names. **Real failure mode** when the experiment runs long enough.

**Gap 2 — Rule (c) "most-recent revision of any protocol-shift series" is fragile.** W4 hygiene prompt would have to read entry text and infer protocol-series membership across multiple entries. Currently only 2 protocols (Human Operator Interaction Protocol, commission-disregarded protocol), each single-revision — manageable. As protocols accumulate revisions over the experiment's life, the inference grows brittle: W4 would need to identify "is this a new protocol or a revision of an existing one?" and "is this the canonical-current revision or a superseded one?" from natural-language entry text. Mechanical hygiene prompts should not depend on natural-language inference.

### Decisions

**Two new factbase files added** to the file-conventions taxonomy:

1. **`Watchlist.md`** — factbase tracking names queued for re-evaluation under specific conditions. Living document; read by all cadences. Sections per strategy. Currently the only structurally-needed section is **Strategy A queue** (names awaiting router-activation re-evaluation). Strategy D pending re-screens NOT in Watchlist.md (calendar events are canonical source); Strategy B prior-NO-GOs NOT in Watchlist.md (B operates on event-flow with fresh-evaluation discipline; sub-pattern factbase preserves the durable signal). Sections may be added as other strategies surface persistent queue needs.

2. **`Operating_Protocols.md`** — canonical reference for active operational protocols (Human Operator Interaction Protocol, commission-disregarded protocol, "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" rule, conviction-calibration ladder, deferral-chaining rules, file-conventions/read-access-scope policy, decision-log lifecycle policy, etc.). Living document; read by all cadences. Each protocol section: title + current canonical text + revision-history pointer list (date + Decision_Log entry pointer + brief change description per revision). When a protocol is revised, new revision text replaces canonical section and prior canonical appended to revision history.

**Rule (c) simplified.** Old form: "Entry is the most-recent revision of a protocol-shift series." New form: "Entry contains canonical-current protocol text NOT YET reflected in `Operating_Protocols.md`." Once W4's PRE-ARCHIVAL MIRRORING step has copied the canonical-current text from a protocol-shift entry to Operating_Protocols.md (with revision-history pointer back to the entry), the entry can archive normally under standard 30-day rule (d). This eliminates the natural-language inference burden — W4 just checks whether the entry's canonical content is reflected in the factbase.

**W4 PRE-ARCHIVAL MIRRORING step inserted.** Before applying lifecycle rules, W4 walks current Decision_Log.md entries and mirrors durable signal into factbases:
- Mirror to Watchlist.md: for any entry that adds a name to a strategy queue, ensure the name appears in Watchlist.md under appropriate strategy section. For any entry that resolves a queue item, ensure resolved name is removed.
- Mirror to Operating_Protocols.md: for any entry that introduces or revises an operational protocol, ensure canonical-current text is reflected.
- After mirroring, contributing entries are eligible for archival under updated rule (c).
- Bootstrap creation handled the same way as Decision_Log_Archive_<YYYY>_<QN>.md and B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md: file created on first need, first lines specified.

**M1 prompt updated to drain Watchlist.md A-queue when router flips ACTIVATE.** Read scope language explicitly states: "M1 maintains Watchlist.md when router-activation calls flip Strategy A from DO-NOT-ACTIVATE to ACTIVATE: trigger fresh thesis-construction sessions for queued names, then remove processed names from Watchlist.md (or hand off to W4 to remove if M1 doesn't process all queued names same-session)." This closes the loop on queue lifecycle.

**Read scopes updated** for D1, W1, W2, M1 to explicitly include the new factbases. Daily/Weekly cadence keeps "live + factbases only" discipline; factbases ARE in scope.

### Explicitly NOT added

- **Closed_Names.md** (would gate fresh evaluation, conflicts with framework's "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" philosophy and "fresh evaluation always allowed" stance). The cost of occasional wasted thesis-construction work on structurally-closed names (e.g., TDOC re-flagged on a fresh ≥5% reaction in 6 months) is accepted; the benefit of preserving framework integrity is paramount.
- **Strategy_B_Watchlist.md** (B's universe is event-flow, not a static queue; sub-pattern factbase preserves durable signal; prior-NO-GO list of 23 names would clutter without operational value).
- **Strategy_D_Watchlist.md** (calendar events are canonical source for D pending re-screens; duplicating to a watchlist file would create consistency-maintenance burden without benefit).
- **Generalizing B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md to other strategies.** D entry-timing-defer NO-GOs are mechanical (rally-roll-off triggers), not pattern-based. A router-gate NO-GOs are regime-conditional, not pattern-based. The B sub-patterns ARE genuine pattern recognition (criterion 4 decisive-flaw types). Asymmetry reflects mechanism asymmetry — don't generalize unnecessarily.

### Compaction-survival note

(a) **Two-factbase addition does NOT change the basic three-tier structure** (Decision_Log live / Decision_Log_Archive / B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy) — it adds two more factbases that ride the same lifecycle pattern: written by W4 maintenance, read by all cadences, contain durable signal extracted from Decision_Log entries that would otherwise be lost on archival.

(b) **Operating_Protocols.md is the more architecturally significant addition.** It moves the framework from "protocols live in Decision_Log entries with W4 inferring revision lineage" to "protocols live in their own document with explicit revision history". Future protocol revisions (e.g., revised conviction-calibration ladder, modified deferral-chaining rules) become cleaner: revise the Operating_Protocols.md section, append revision history entry, write a Decision_Log entry summarizing the change, let the Decision_Log entry archive normally at 30 days. No "find the most-recent revision among scattered entries" inference required.

(c) **Watchlist.md is the more operationally significant addition.** Without it, the Strategy A queue (CAT/LLY/QCOM/AAPL) is genuinely at risk of being lost when session-end consolidation entries archive ~2026-06-02. With it, the queue is a stable factbase that all Daily/Weekly/Monthly sessions can read, and M1 has explicit drainage responsibility when router flips ACTIVATE.

(d) **First W4 run is now further expanded.** Per prior compaction-survival notes, first W4 run already had to bootstrap Decision_Log_Archive_2026_Q2.md and B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md from current Decision_Log entries. With Part 5, it also bootstraps Watchlist.md (extracting current A-queue) and Operating_Protocols.md (extracting current canonical protocols). Bootstrap workload is concentrated in the first run; steady-state runs are much lighter.

(e) **The "fix as you see fit" instruction is not standing authorization for unilateral framework changes.** This session's Part 5 changes were narrowly scoped to closing two specific gaps that operator-probing had surfaced. Future open-ended "fix" instructions should similarly be interpreted in the context of explicitly-surfaced gaps rather than as broad design discretion. Strategy.md and Experiment_Parameters.md immutability locks remain in force; Claude_Task_Plan.md modifications are the only operational-document edits in scope.

(f) **Operator communication-style observation:** The operator's question pattern ("do we have X?", "is it Y?", "do we have anything for Z?") consistently probes for gaps without prescribing solutions. The pattern is "surface the gap, then authorize the fix." Future sessions should expect operator probing to converge on a "fix as you see fit" turn after 2-4 question turns — and should use the question turns to map gap dimensions accurately so the eventual fix is well-targeted.

### Why criterion 4 fails decisively (information-driven vs sentiment-driven attacker check)

Per Strategy.md criterion 4: "attacker must consider whether the market reaction is information-driven rather than sentiment-driven (if information-driven, 'mispricing' is actually correct pricing)." Attacker's case for information-driven:

1. **Pre-print PT cluster priced-in forward narrative.** Mizuho $217 / MS $217 / TD Cowen $215 + prior raises UBS $259 / Guggenheim $220 establish a pre-print PT cluster with mean ~$226. Trefis pre-FDA-approval explicit framing: "$9 billion valuation appears to have largely priced in a positive outcome." Pre-print stock $188.99 was below the cluster mean by ~$37 reflecting modest residual upside from PT cluster — but this is normal post-FDA-approval discount, not undershoot.

2. **Post-print stock at PT consensus.** Mon 5/4 close ~$227.93 lands AT/modestly-above the pre-print PT cluster mean ~$226 and the consensus range $221-228. This is the diagnostic signature of sell-side-correctly-priced reaction: stock closes where analysts said it should be after the print, not above (would indicate sentiment overshoot) and not below (would indicate undershoot). This signature is shared with CBOE 2026-05-02 (post-print $319.74 at Piper $321) — direct sub-pattern 3 match.

3. **Q1 print's information content reinforces the forward narrative.** Revenue/EPS misses are quantitatively small relative to the forward narrative dominator (Auvelity AD agitation launch June). Volume metric (+35% Y/Y prescriptions) provides positive forward-execution evidence. Sales force expansion to ~630 reps confirms launch-ramp infrastructure investment. The print's content is APPROXIMATELY INFORMATION-NEUTRAL relative to pre-print expectations: financial misses are partially priced and forward-narrative confirmations are within expected range. The +20% close-to-close move is therefore best explained by FDA-approval-positive-catalyst absorption (the Apr 30 approval was Day -2 ago, and the launch ramp is now inside the 60-day window) rather than print-driven re-rating beyond information content.

4. **Trailing-momentum context confirms pre-print rally was not undershoot.** Trailing-12-mo +72% + trailing-1-month +14-15% pre-FDA-approval establishes that AXSM was already in a multi-period bullish-rally state going into the print. There is no evidence of recent price suppression (no IBM-style NOW + IGV cascade-suppression event); to the contrary, the stock was at multi-month highs entering the print on already-priced-in approval expectations.

5. **Sector/peer context does not support undershoot.** Health Care sector context per Daily.md 2026-05-04: HCA holds existing B position with peer-corroboration thesis; no broad biotech-mean-reversion-from-overshoot pattern visible. AXSM's reaction is idiosyncratic (Auvelity launch context) not sector-driven.

**Attacker conclusion: reaction is information-driven; "mispricing" thesis fails. Criterion 4 fails decisively.**

**LONG framing dismissal:** No undershoot setup exists. Market is correctly pricing forward-positive narrative. Buying at $227.93 against a PT cluster mean ~$226 means buying at PT-cluster-pricing rather than at undershoot — no asymmetric-upside-anchor for B's mean-reversion mechanism to capture.

**SHORT framing dismissal:** Three compounding criterion 4 decisive flaws:

(a) **Was the criterion 4 sub-pattern 3 routing applied correctly given the FDA-approval-launch-context overlay?** Yes. SBUX and CBOE precedents established sub-pattern 3 as "pre-print PT raises absorb expectations + post-print stock at PT consensus + sell-side mild PT response." AXSM matches all three diagnostics: pre-print PT cluster mean ~$226 absorbed forward narrative; post-print close ~$227.93 at the cluster; post-print PT actions not yet documented but structurally consistent with mild response (Daily.md scan filtered to ≥$50B mkt caps which AXSM at $11B is below). This is consistent with the KL flag from the prior 2026-05-02 AXSM NO-GO compaction-survival note ("would have routed to SBUX-style sub-pattern NO-GO if evaluated") which explicitly anticipated this routing.

(b) **Could the AD agitation launch June 2026 be classified as STLA-style sub-pattern 5 in-window-binary-catalyst?** Considered. Counter: AD agitation launch is a SOFT catalyst — gradual prescription ramp, sales force deployment, marketing campaigns, no single-day binary event with mechanical disposition like Investor Day or PDUFA decision. STLA's Investor Day was May 21 with binary new-strategy-presentation event. AXSM's AD launch is execution-quality-dependent over multi-month horizon. (c) **Was the criterion 1 measurement-precision uncertainty (+10-11% per Daily.md vs +20.6% from binding Fri-to-Mon close-to-close) addressed correctly?** Yes. Both plausible references clear ≥5% threshold by 2-4x cushion. The disposition does not depend on which reference is binding. Daily.md scan-stage phrasing inconsistency flagged for future Daily-scan refinement (similar to AXSM 2026-05-02 premarket-vs-regular-session refinement flagged in EQIX/AXSM compaction-survival pattern).

(d) **Could a LONG-only framing recover the disposition via "FDA-approval-launch-tailwind continues to drive upside through 60-day window"?** No. That framing would be Strategy A (catalyst-driven thesis on upcoming catalyst's execution outcome) not Strategy B (mean-reversion from event-reaction mispricing). AXSM does not fit either Strategy A or Strategy B; the LONG-framing-via-Strategy-B fails on absent undershoot anchor as documented above.

(e) **Was the prior 2026-05-02 AXSM NO-GO criterion 1 disposition revisited?** No, and it should not be — that disposition addressed the FDA-approval event (Apr 30) close-to-close magnitude failure. Today's NO-GO addresses the Q1-print event (Mon 5/4) which is a structurally distinct event with its own 10-day entry window. Per Operating Protocols "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" rule, fresh-event-driven re-trigger merits fresh thesis-construction evaluation; this session is that evaluation. (f) **Was deferral considered?** No. Criterion 4 disposition is structural and data-stable. No additional information (e.g., post-print PT raises in coming days, AD launch progress updates, peer biotech reactions) would resolve the binding constraint (sub-pattern 3 information-priced-via-pre-print-rally + sub-pattern-4-mirror in-window-positive-catalyst + KL #2.20 textbook-rational-trap on short framing). Deferral would just delay the same NO-GO disposition while consuming entry-window time.

(g) **Was the "double-NO-GO on same name in 4 days" pattern examined for over-rejection bias?** Yes. AXSM's two NO-GOs are at structurally distinct mechanical layers (criterion 1 vs criterion 4) and address two distinct triggering events (FDA approval Apr 30 vs Q1 print May 4). The first NO-GO was MECHANICAL (close-to-close magnitude); the second NO-GO is STRATEGIC (information-pricing diagnostic). Both NO-GOs are independently grounded — the second NO-GO does not depend on the first being correct, and the sub-pattern 3 routing would have applied to the AXSM Q1-print case independent of any prior name-specific session. The "double-NO-GO" framing is a coincidence of two distinct events on the same name within the same 10-day window, not evidence of over-rejection bias.

### Decision

**NCLH — NO-GO (DECLINE) on dual-framing analysis. LONG framing fails on absent mean-reversion anchor: the FY26 guide cut ~30% midpoint crystallizes pre-existing structural macro overhangs (Iran-war fuel costs ongoing since June 2025; European consumer/booking weakness multi-quarter pre-existing), and the binding refutation pathway requires either (a) macro-condition reversal (Iran ceasefire announcement; EU consumer recovery signal), (b) Q2 2026 print at-or-just-outside 60-day window (NCLH Q2 typically reports late July / early August; 60-day window from May 5 entry expires ~Jul 4 → outside window), or (c) competitor prints (CCL Q2 late June / RCL Q2 late July) providing partial signal but only partially within window. Cross-name RCL -2.3% / CCL-weaker confirm sector-wide structural-information-driven reading rather than single-name sentiment overshoot. The magnitude analysis (-8.56% price move on -32% EPS guide cut = market is being measured not panicky, implying ~28% of the cut absorbed as price-reflected forward expectation OR cycle-low-confidence pricing FY27 recovery) does not provide a clean sentiment-overshoot anchor because the magnitude is plausibly information-correct given the macro-driver durability. SHORT framing fails on Strategy B mechanism mismatch: per BE/CAT/TWLO/UPS precedent, "arguing further downside via mean-reversion to a lower PT cluster is structurally a momentum-continuation thesis (Strategy A territory, not B)" — sell-side will likely cluster PT cuts down from current consensus toward new-guide-justified levels, which is the OPPOSITE of mean-reversion-toward-PT-cluster; pre-mortem KL #1 textbook-rational-trap 2.20 is active (shorting after a sharp negative move where sell-side will ratify the cut would punish 2.20 directly); KL #7 short-side gap-up execution risk is also active in the current geopolitical-tape regime (Iran/Hormuz Project Freedom escalation since prior Decision_Log entries — same active-gap-regime that informed UPS yesterday).** Sub-pattern 4 advances 3 → 4 instances (V/MDLZ variant 4a, UPS variant 4b, NCLH variant 4c) with NCLH establishing new variant 4c "guide-cut-on-pre-existing-macro-overhang" — distinguishing feature is print-as-catalyst-with-hard-FY26-guide-CUT-crystallizing-pre-existing-macro-overhang vs variant 4a print-confirms-overhang-with-guide-REAFFIRMED (V/MDLZ) and variant 4b new-overhang-emergence-at-non-print-catalyst (UPS). Criterion 1 mechanically clears with substantial cushion (close-to-close -8.56% = 1.7x cushion vs ≥5% threshold). Instrument eligibility clears with material cushion (mkt cap ~$7B = 3.5x $2B floor; volume 134%-above-3mo on print-day implies multi-billion-dollar ADV well above $10M floor). Criterion 5 cleared (no A position open; not in C either per cross-strategy holding check).

### LONG framing dismissal

The mean-reversion thesis would require: market overreacted to the guide cut, and structural drivers fade or are refuted within 60 days. Three weights examined; LONG fails decisively:

(1) **Magnitude analysis does not support overshoot.** -8.56% price move on -32% EPS guide cut = market absorbing roughly 28% of the cut into price (assuming static multiple). For a sentiment-overshoot LONG thesis, market should be absorbing >100% of the rational-pricing magnitude (overshoot). Actual absorption is well below 100%, suggesting market is being measured. Alternative read: market is partially absorbing the cut + partially pricing FY27 cyclical recovery (cruise demand structurally strong; multi-year capacity buildout) — but this read implies the market is correctly pricing not overshooting.

(2) **No in-window binding refutation pathway.** NCLH Q2 2026 print is the natural binding refutation event (would either confirm new guide or revise) but lands ~late July / early August = outside the 60-day window from May 5 entry (window expires ~Jul 4). Macro-driver reversal (Iran ceasefire; EU consumer recovery) is plausible but uncertain on 60-day timeline — the active geopolitical-tape regime (Iran/Hormuz Project Freedom escalation flagged in UPS NO-GO yesterday) suggests fuel-cost overhang is persistent at minimum through the window. Competitor prints provide only partial signal: CCL fiscal Q2 reports late June (within window) but cruise lines have idiosyncratic exposure differences; RCL Q2 late July (outside window). No clean Strategy B closed-list catalyst within window.

(3) **Sell-side trajectory pending DOWN-revision, not UP.** Pre-event PT consensus stale-pre-guide-cut. Sell-side will likely cluster PT cuts down from current toward new-guide-justified levels over the next 5-10 trading days. PT cuts ratify the move rather than enable mean-reversion. The "implied upside to PT cluster" anchor that supports a LONG thesis is mostly stale and will revise down. This is the V/MDLZ pattern (sub-pattern 4 variant 4a) extended to harder-guide-cut form (variant 4c).

### SHORT framing dismissal

(1) **Strategy B mechanism mismatch.** Per BE/CAT/TWLO/UPS precedent doctrine: "arguing further downside via mean-reversion to a lower PT cluster is structurally a momentum-continuation thesis (Strategy A territory, not B)." Strategy B's mechanism is mean-reversion from sentiment-overshoot, not momentum-continuation post-structural-information-event.

(2) **KL #1 textbook-rational-trap 2.20 active.** Shorting after a sharp negative move on a hard-information event (FY26 guide cut on macro drivers) would punish 2.20 directly — the textbook-rational thesis is "stock should fall further toward new-guide-implied fair value" but B's selectivity discipline penalizes textbook-rational entries.

(3) **KL #7 short-side gap-up execution risk in active geopolitical regime.** Iran/Hormuz Project Freedom escalation introduces non-thesis-related gap-up risk (sudden Iran ceasefire announcement = sharp short squeeze in a fuel-sensitive name like NCLH). Same regime that informed UPS NO-GO yesterday. NCLH cyclical-discretionary names are particularly gap-prone in this regime.

### Sub-pattern routing — sub-pattern 4 variant 4c "guide-cut-on-pre-existing-macro-overhang" established

**Primary characterization: sub-pattern 4 with new variant 4c.** Mechanism shared with variants 4a (V/MDLZ) and 4b (UPS): structural overhang requiring multi-quarter resolution lands on the binding fundamental concern; the post-event reaction is information-driven (not sentiment-overshoot) because the overhang is empirically-grounded; mean-reversion-from-overshoot is unavailable because the post-event price reflects new overhang-adjusted fair value; SHORT extension-toward-pending-PT-cuts is structurally inappropriate for Strategy B's mean-reversion mechanism (Strategy A territory).

**Variant 4c distinguishing features** (vs 4a / 4b):
1. **Catalyst is the print itself (like 4a, unlike 4b).** Q1 2026 earnings print Mon 5/4 BMO is the catalyst event.
2. **Print contains a HARD GUIDE CUT (unlike 4a where guide was reaffirmed; unlike 4b where there was no print at the catalyst).** FY26 EPS midpoint -32%; FY26 EBITDA midpoint -8.9%. The guide cut crystallizes the magnitude of pre-existing macro overhangs, providing hard-information confirmation that prior pre-print bearish positioning had been TOO BULLISH on FY26 ($2.38 EPS guide stale).
3. **Overhang source is external macro (like MDLZ cocoa-cost; unlike UPS competitive-moat-erosion).** Iran-war fuel costs (ongoing since June 2025) + weak European bookings (multi-quarter EU consumer overhang). Both are external macro factors, not company-specific competitive failures.
4. **Pre-existing overhang (like 4a; unlike 4b).** The fuel-cost and EU-weakness overhangs were known pre-print; the print did not introduce the overhangs but crystallized their FY26 magnitude via the guide cut.
5. **Cross-name sympathy partial (like 4b; unlike 4a).** RCL -2.3% / CCL weaker confirms sector-coordinated reading but at attenuated magnitude (NCLH bears the direct hit; peers absorb sympathy). Variant 4a (V/MDLZ) had limited cross-name sympathy because the overhangs were name-specific (V regulatory; MDLZ cocoa is industry-shared but other shelf-stable names didn't move much). Variant 4b (UPS) had strong cross-name sympathy (FDX -9.5%, ODFL -5.7%) reflecting the sector-wide competitive threat.

**Variant 4c pattern signature for Daily.md scan-stage recognition:** if a candidate exhibits (a) a sharp negative-direction post-event move on an earnings-print catalyst with (b) a HARD FY-guide CUT (≥15% midpoint for at least one major guide line), AND (c) cited drivers are external macro factors (commodity-cost shock, geopolitical event affecting input costs, macro consumer/end-market weakness), AND (d) cross-name sympathy in same sector (read-across), AND (e) the binding macro factor's resolution requires macro-condition reversal not earnings recovery alone — classify as variant 4c NO-GO without requiring full thesis-construction depth. Full thesis-construction depth warranted only if (i) the magnitude analysis suggests clean overshoot (e.g., move >100% of rational-pricing magnitude implied by guide cut), (ii) a specific in-window Strategy B closed-list catalyst is identifiable that would mechanically resolve the binding macro concern, OR (iii) the cross-name sympathy reading is ambiguous (would suggest single-name sentiment overshoot).

### Considered alternative routings

**(A) Sub-pattern 6 valuation-reset-but-not-narrative-reset (TEAM precedent).** Considered. Counter: TEAM's case was that the print delivered a multiple-compression-only event (valuation reset but underlying narrative — growth, margin trajectory — intact). NCLH's guide cut is direct earnings-power damage on FY26, not just multiple compression. The new EPS guide $1.45-$1.79 vs prior $2.38 is hard earnings-trajectory revision, not multiple-driven. TEAM-pattern not applicable.

**(B) Sub-pattern 5 in-window-binary-catalyst (STLA precedent).** Considered. Counter: STLA's case had a specific binary disclosure event (Investor Day May 21) that would mechanically resolve the binding constraint within window. NCLH has no such binary in-window event — Q2 print is outside window; macro reversal is uncertain. STLA-pattern not applicable.

**(C) Sub-pattern 1 cleanest-L1-instance / sub-pattern 2 INTC-pattern.** Both are positive-direction sub-patterns; NCLH is negative-direction. Not applicable.

**(D) Sub-pattern 3 information-priced-via-pre-print-rally.** Considered. Counter: sub-pattern 3 requires the post-print stock to land AT pre-raised PT cluster confirming sell-side fair-value-shifted-up. NCLH had no pre-print PT raises — the move is DOWN with PT cuts forward-pending. Not applicable.

**Conclusion: variant 4c is the cleanest available routing.** Direct precedent on core mechanism (V/MDLZ/UPS sub-pattern 4 multi-quarter-resolution-vs-60-day-window mismatch); variant distinguishing features (hard-guide-cut + macro-source + pre-existing) are genuinely structurally distinct from existing variants and provide useful taxonomic granularity for future Daily.md scan-stage recognition.

### Theater-check (brief)

(a) **Could the magnitude analysis (only 8.56% on 32% guide cut) actually indicate sentiment-undershoot LONG anchor?** Examined. Counter: cyclical-consumer-discretionary cruise lines have high operational leverage and often trade with FY27-recovery-implied multiples even during cyclical lows. The 8.56% absorption rate is plausibly explained by FY27-recovery-pricing rather than sentiment-undershoot. Even if some sentiment overshoot exists, the binding refutation pathways (macro reversal; Q2 print outside window) do not exist within 60 days, so even a marginal sentiment component cannot rationally produce a Strategy B mean-reversion entry. NO-GO holds.

(b) **Was the criterion 4 dual-framing test applied correctly?** Yes. LONG framing tested on three weights (magnitude, in-window refutation pathway, sell-side trajectory) — all fail. SHORT framing tested on three established doctrines (Strategy A territory, KL #1 trap, KL #7 gap risk) — all fail. Both framings fail at independently-grounded decisive flaws.

(c) **Was variant 4c establishment justified or forced?** Genuinely structurally distinct. The hard-guide-cut + pre-existing-macro-overhang combination is meaningfully different from 4a (guide-reaffirmed) and 4b (non-print-catalyst-with-no-guide-update). Variant naming makes future pattern recognition more precise (NCLH-class candidates can be filtered earlier in the funnel).

(d) **Was deferral considered?** No. Criterion 4 disposition is structural and data-stable. Deferring would not change the disposition (the binding constraints are not resolvable by additional information within the 10-day post-event entry window). Per Operating Protocols, deferrals do not chain and the conservative default is NO-GO; deferring would just delay the same disposition while consuming entry-window time.

### Conviction calibration

**HIGH conviction in NO-GO disposition (~80-85%).** Sub-pattern 4 routing is direct-precedent-supported across 3 prior instances (V, MDLZ, UPS). The new variant 4c adds rather than weakens precedent strength — NCLH's hard-guide-cut signal is structurally stronger evidence of information-driven repricing than V/MDLZ's guide-reaffirmation cases (the cut itself is the binding new information). Both LONG framing (no mean-reversion anchor; no in-window convergence; pending PT cuts down) and SHORT framing (Strategy A territory + KL #1 + KL #7) fail independently at decisive flaws. There is no plausible Strategy B framing that survives criterion 4 attacker check. Disposition is mechanism-resolved, not borderline.

### Decision

**CRCL — NO-GO (DECLINE) on dual-framing analysis. Criterion 4 fails decisively on multiple compounding flaws, primary routing sub-pattern 5 in-window-binary-catalyst.** Mechanical eligibility cleared with material cushion: criterion 1 +16% close-to-close = 3.2x cushion vs ≥5% threshold; instrument eligibility mkt cap ~$24B = 12x $2B floor + multi-hundred-million-dollar ADV well above $10M floor (CRCL ~11 months post-IPO, NYSE common, fractional support assumed at this maturity); criterion 5 cleared (no A position; not in C). Criterion 3 has Q1 print May 11 as a closed-list-eligible event-anchor, but the print itself IS the binding binary catalyst against criterion 4, not a directional convergence target.

### LONG framing dismissal (momentum-continuation = Strategy A territory)

The +16% positive-direction move on hard regulatory-clarity information has the canonical momentum-continuation profile: pre-event PT consensus $127.24 already implied upside vs pre-event price ~$101.5 (~25% pre-event undervaluation); post-event PT consensus $136.56 implies further +16% upside from post-event price ~$117.7. A LONG thesis would be "drift up to consensus PT $136 over coming weeks" — this is structurally Strategy A's mandate (entering a name with directional thesis on continuation toward catalyst-driven fair value), not Strategy B's mean-reversion-from-overshoot mandate. Per established BE/CAT/TWLO/UPS doctrine: "arguing further drift toward higher PT cluster is structurally a momentum-continuation thesis (Strategy A territory, not B)." The Daily.md prompt's framing of "B opportunity for upside drift to consensus" is a category-error — drift-to-consensus is continuation, not mean-reversion. Pre-mortem KL #1 textbook-rational-trap 2.20 active on the LONG side: chasing momentum to PT consensus after a sharp positive event is the textbook-rational instinct B is designed to penalize.

### SHORT framing dismissal (absent overshoot anchor + sub-pattern 5 + KL #7)

The SHORT mean-reversion thesis (Strategy B's natural direction on +16% positive moves: bet retracement back toward pre-event reference $101.5) fails on three independently-decisive grounds:

(1) **Sub-pattern 5 in-window-binary-catalyst — DECISIVE alone.** Q1 2026 print Mon 2026-05-11 BMO is at T+5 trading days from Tue 5/5 entry (week 2 of holding period). Senate Banking Committee CLARITY-Act markup expected week of May 11, T+5 to T+9 trading days. **Both binaries land in the same week, deep within the 60-day window (~10–15% into the window).** Strategy B's mechanism is "60-day mean-reversion as the market digests realized event narrative" — this requires the 60-day window to be dominated by narrative-digestion drift, NOT by stacked binary catalysts in week 2. The Q1 print specifically will produce a large move in either direction (USDC market-cap growth + transaction volume + revenue trajectory + forward guidance on regulatory-impact-on-margins — none of which is currently priced because the regulatory framework just changed Mon 5/4). The Senate Banking markup will produce a binary legislative outcome (advance favorably / stall / contentious) that further uncouples from any mean-reversion thesis. Holding the position through week 2 effectively makes it a bet on the joint distribution of these binaries, NOT on the +16% mean-reversion thesis. Per STLA precedent: Strategy B "is explicitly designed for evaluating the quality of a realized market reaction to known public information, rather than predicting a future event's outcome — the CRCL setup forces the latter."

(2) **Absent overshoot magnitude anchor.** Pre-event PT consensus $127.24 vs pre-event price ~$101.5 = ~25% pre-event undervaluation already implied by sell-side. Post-event price ~$117.7 = $9.54 BELOW consensus PT $127.24 = 8% gap-to-consensus remaining. Post-event PT raised to $136.56 implies +16% further upside. The +16% move is therefore PARTIAL pricing of the regulatory tailwind, NOT overshoot — closer to undershoot vs new fair value. SHORT mean-reversion thesis requires overshoot evidence (move > rational-pricing magnitude); CRCL shows the OPPOSITE. BofA Mon 5/4 sector-bullish commentary ("net positive across bank sub-sectors") + Polymarket CLARITY-Act-signed-2026 odds jumping to 61% confirm hard-information-pricing not sentiment-overshoot. (3) **KL #7 short-side gap-up execution risk amplified by stacked binaries + KL #1 textbook-rational-trap.** Q1 print + Senate markup both create gap-up risk in week 2: favorable Q1 + favorable markup → sharp short-squeeze gap-up, breaching B's +25% short stop with high probability. ### Sub-pattern routing — sub-pattern 5 with new variant 5b "stacked-near-term-binaries"

**Primary characterization: sub-pattern 5 in-window-binary-catalyst (STLA precedent, 2nd instance with new variant).** Mechanism shared with STLA: a known scheduled binary catalyst lands inside the 60-day window and uncouples from the mean-reversion thesis, forcing the position to be a bet on the catalyst outcome rather than narrative-digestion drift.

**Variant 5b distinguishing features** (vs STLA variant 5a):
1. **STLA variant 5a "single-strategic-disclosure-event mid-window"**: Investor Day May 21 at T+17 trading days from notional May 4 entry, ~28% into 60-day window; SINGLE company-specific strategic disclosure that supersedes Q1 narrative.
2. **CRCL variant 5b "stacked-near-term-binaries early-window"**: Q1 print Mon May 11 BMO at T+5 trading days + Senate Banking markup week of May 11 at T+5–9 trading days; STACKED fundamental-binary + political-binary in the SAME WEEK at ~10–15% into the 60-day window. The stacking creates compounded gap risk and dominates week-2 pricing entirely; mean-reversion drift cannot operate when two binaries fire simultaneously near entry.

**Variant 5b pattern signature for Daily.md scan-stage recognition:** if a candidate exhibits (a) sharp post-event move + (b) two or more known scheduled binary catalysts within first 2 weeks of the 60-day window (e.g., earnings print + legislative/regulatory event; product launch + court ruling), AND (c) the binaries are uncorrelated to the entry catalyst's narrative — classify as variant 5b NO-GO without requiring full thesis-construction depth. Full thesis-construction depth warranted only if (i) one or more binaries can be argued to mechanically resolve toward the mean-reversion thesis (e.g., earnings print expected to undercut the entry-catalyst narrative quantitatively), (ii) the binaries are mutually offsetting in expected direction (rare), OR (iii) the binaries occur outside week 2 (later within window allows narrative-drift to begin).

### Considered alternative routings

**(A) Sub-pattern 1 cleanest-positive-direction-L1 (NXPI/STX/CAT precedent).** Considered as primary. Counter: CRCL has the sub-pattern 1 features (positive-direction event + sell-side ratification emerging + cross-name sympathy) BUT the in-window-binary-catalyst issue is more decisive and more proximate to the entry decision. Sub-pattern 5 routing is structurally more decisive because the binaries occur AT the entry-window edge, dominating week-2 pricing. Sub-pattern 1 documented as secondary feature of the disposition; primary routing remains sub-pattern 5.

**(B) Sub-pattern 4 variant 4c guide-cut-on-pre-existing-macro-overhang (NCLH precedent).** Not applicable. CRCL is positive-direction with regulatory tailwind; sub-pattern 4 covers negative-direction structural-overhang scenarios.

**(C) Sub-pattern 6 valuation-reset-but-not-narrative-reset (TEAM precedent).** Not applicable. CRCL move is narrative-driven (regulatory tailwind clarifies thesis), not multiple-compression-only.

**(D) Direct LONG entry under "criterion-3 closed-list event-anchor with Q1 print as convergence event".** Considered. Counter: criterion 3 closed-list permits "next earnings release" as event-anchor for convergence, but criterion 4 attacker check overrides — Q1 print IS the binary catalyst that creates the criterion-4 decisive flaw. Using the binary as both convergence anchor and criterion-4-defeating-binary is internally inconsistent: a convergence event in B's framework means the position resolves at the event with quality assessed against the event's outcome; here the event itself is what makes the entry inappropriate. STLA precedent: "Strategy B is explicitly designed for evaluating the quality of a realized market reaction to known public information, rather than predicting a future event's outcome." Q1 print is the future event whose outcome would be the dominant driver — STLA-doctrine applies.

**Conclusion: variant 5b is the cleanest available routing.** STLA established sub-pattern 5 as the in-window-binary-catalyst category; CRCL extends to stacked-near-term-binaries variant. Direct precedent on core mechanism.

### Compaction-survival notes for future Claude

(a) **The Daily.md "Strategy B long-only" framing error is precedent-setting for future scans.** Strategy.md Strategy B instrument eligibility is "Long or short." Future Daily.md scans should categorize negative-direction post-event ≥5% moves as B-short candidates with explicit framework reference (acknowledging B-short structural exposure to KL #1 textbook-rational-trap and KL #7 short-side gap-up execution risk) rather than "no action under long-only" framing. The decline disposition for SHOP/PYPL/CDW today is regime-based not framework-based; this distinction matters for future sessions if regime tightens (VIX ≥20 / SPY Trend NEUTRAL or DOWN) and B-short framing becomes more attractive.

(b) **B short-direction in current regime: implicit deferral until regime tightens.** The 6+ consecutive B-short NO-GO precedent string (BE/CAT/TWLO/UPS/NCLH/CRCL) plus the Iran-de-escalation risk-on tape with SPX/Nasdaq/Russell concurrent ATH establishes high prior against B-short framings. This is not a permanent veto — VIX rising above 20 / SPY Trend flipping to NEUTRAL or DOWN would shift the regime context. Future Daily.md scans surfacing B-short candidates should explicitly check current regime and the recent NO-GO precedent string before routing to thesis-construction.

(c) **Qualifying-event sub-test for criterion 1 is mechanical-but-not-trivially-mechanical.** MU sell-side commentary (third-party) cleanly fails. AMD/FLEX/DOC/ARM/SMCI/UBER earnings prints (with-or-without guidance) cleanly clear. GLW strategic-customer-partnership-announcement is borderline — first-party but not on the explicit list. NVO 340B-reversal-noise creates magnitude borderline rather than event borderline. The sub-test requires both event-type classification AND magnitude verification at close-to-close on event day; partial-day or non-close-to-close measurements (e.g., +15% intraday Tue for PINS that may or may not have held) require thesis-construction-time verification. Future Daily.md scan-stage classification benefits from being explicit about "first-party event vs third-party commentary" alongside magnitude.

(d) **Watchlist.md architecture as state-index, not queue.** Per the 2026-05-04 factbase-architecture decision and reinforced today, Watchlist.md captures (i) Strategy A queue (genuine queue with router-flip resolution); (ii) state-index audit trail for B disqualifier-flag and short-direction-declined-at-D2 items; (iii) D re-screen pipeline pointers (canonical tracking via calendar events). ### Decisions

**Trigger condition verification (mechanical, all three required):**

(a) **MET (with substantial margin).** Q2 FY26 Entertainment SVOD operating margin **10.6%** vs Q1 FY26 8.4% baseline = +220bps QoQ; cleared the 8.4% reaffirmation sub-condition; **also** cleared the FY26 10% guide directional reaffirmation sub-condition (Q2 print itself exceeded the full-year guide line). Streaming OI $582M vs prior management Q2 guide $500M = +16% above own guide. Disney CEO statement (Q2 8-K Ex-99.1): "we delivered our first double-digit Entertainment SVOD operating margin in Q2 and remain on track to deliver at least 10% for the full fiscal year 2026."

(b) **MET.** D'Amaro debut earnings call (May 6, 8:30 AM ET) framed strategic continuity, not strategic reset. Three-pillar framework (per shareholder letter and Q2 8-K Section "OUR STRATEGY"): (1) investing in IP and creativity that breaks through, builds connections, and endures; (2) reaching more consumers in more seamless, engaging ways around the world; (3) using advanced technologies to power our storytelling and increase monetization and returns. D'Amaro statement (Q1 transcript via Motley Fool): "what I'm focused on is executing on the priorities that we've already communicated to the market" + "we're focused on creating best-in-class content...strengthening our streaming businesses...continuing to take advantage of the growing power of live sports and build ESPN's direct-to-consumer business...turbocharging Disney experiences" — explicit continuation of Iger-era priorities. CFO Johnston (per CNBC): "the company isn't anticipating any changes to adjusted earnings growth expectations for fiscal 2026 or 2027 in light of gas prices or consumer spending." Internal Disney letter framing "One Disney" as cross-divisional synergy (per Cinemablend Q2 live blog) is consolidation-of-existing-architecture language, not strategic-pivot language. No personnel turnover announcements; CFO Johnston (operational anchor) continues; Iger transitions to advisor through YE 2026 per prior succession plan. **No major strategic pivot signaling early-tenure reset risk.**

(c) **MET (and exceeded).** FY26 buyback target **raised** from $7B (prior pace) to **at least $8B** (per Q2 8-K Ex-99.1 explicit guide: "We are targeting at least $8 billion in share repurchases in fiscal 2026"). $1B raise = +14% above prior pace. Trigger required reaffirmation; outcome was acceleration. FY27 double-digit adj EPS growth additionally guided.

**All three trigger conditions MET.** Fresh Strategy D thesis construction initiated per session-prompt step 4 with explicit Subtype B reframing of primary driver from management-execution-quality (the original NO-GO basis) to financial-metric-traceable (the structurally-required Subtype B framing).

**Strategy D entry criteria 1-6 evaluation (Subtype B framing):**

**Criterion 1 — Structural thesis with 12+ month expected realization timeline.** Subtype B trend-continuation thesis. **Primary driver (financial-metric-traceable, NOT management-execution-quality):** Entertainment SVOD operating margin sustained at ≥10% over 12+ months, anchored to two-quarter trend-evidence in hand: Q1 FY26 = 8.4%, Q2 FY26 = 10.6%, FY26 management guide = "at least 10%" reaffirmed by Q2 results, FY27 framing implies continued double-digit margin. Compounding metrics (secondary-supporting, NOT primary): FY26 adj EPS growth ~12% ex-53rd-week / ~16% incl. 53rd-week reaffirmed; FY27 double-digit adj EPS growth guided; FY26 buyback ≥$8B (raised from $7B) with $19B FY26 cash from operations target reaffirmed. Multi-year trend-realization window: 4-6 forward quarters of margin-trajectory verification (next read Q3 FY26 print ~2026-08-12 per TradingView next-earnings-date) plus Experiences segment OI continuation as secondary read-through.

**Reframing rationale (per session-prompt step 4 explicit requirement).** The original 2026-04-26 NO-GO cited two compounding criterion-4 issues: (i) Strategy D thesis category for DIS in Quarterly_D_Candidates.md was "Management execution" (Category 3) — exactly the residual pre-mortem rev 5 KL #4 flags ("management-execution outcomes are the hardest to falsify in advance and the most prone to narrative-vs-results decoupling"); (ii) Subtype B trend-metric was single-quarter-anchored at Q1 FY26 8.4% only, with second observation pending the May 6 print, making the trend-continuation framing structurally premature. Both issues are now structurally resolved: the Q2 print provides the second observation (8.4% → 10.6%, trend-direction confirmed, magnitude within management-guided trajectory), AND the primary driver of the thesis is REFRAMED from "D'Amaro will execute the Iger strategy well" (a subjective management-execution-quality assessment subject to KL #4 residual) to "Entertainment SVOD operating margin will sustain at ≥10% for 12+ forward months and FY26 adj EPS growth will hit ~12% reaffirmed level" (a quantitative financial-metric trajectory subject to public-document-observable invalidation). KL #4 residual remains acknowledged as a SECONDARY driver at the thesis level: management execution quality is a contributing factor that ultimately manifests in the financial metrics, but the thesis is anchored to the metrics, not to the management-quality assessment. If D'Amaro fails operationally and the failure manifests in margin breach or EPS guide cut, invalidation criteria (i)/(ii) trip mechanically. If D'Amaro fails operationally but financial metrics keep holding via inertia / legacy-trajectory / parks compensation, the thesis would technically remain "valid" until a metric breach surfaces — this is the KL #4 residual under Subtype B framing, accepted as architectural property rather than fixable defect, partially mitigated by the 2-consecutive-quarter requirement on the primary invalidation gate (preventing single-quarter outlier from auto-invalidating but ensuring sustained breach trips).

**Criterion 2 — Thesis constructed from primary-source materials.** Q2 FY26 8-K Ex-99.1 (SEC EDGAR `fy2026_q2xprxex991.htm`); Q2 FY26 earnings call transcript (Motley Fool, full text); D'Amaro shareholder letter (Q2 8-K Ex-99 OUR STRATEGY section + thewaltdisneycompany.com news posting); Q1 FY26 8-K Ex-99 (Q1 SVOD baseline, FY26 guide first issuance, succession framing — referenced via prior Quarterly_D_Candidates.md screen); FY25 10-K (Q4 calendar year 2025 results, Sep fiscal year-end metrics); FY24 10-K (Iger return-to-CEO context, succession-architecture framework continuity). Sector context: NFLX as structural streaming-margin leader (Q4 2025 ~30% margin reference), PSKY (Paramount-Skydance) restructuring noise, WBD streaming-margin-trajectory comparison; theme parks sector context vs CMCSA Universal. **Criterion 3 — Adversarial counter-argument addressing multi-year risks.**

(α) **Management turnover risk.** D'Amaro is 7 weeks into tenure (CEO effective March 18, 2026). The thesis's KL #4 residual under Subtype B reframing (above Criterion 1) bounds this risk to financial-metric breach rather than subjective execution-quality assessment. CFO Johnston's continued tenure provides operational continuity through transition. Iger transitions to advisor through YE 2026 per disclosed succession architecture; not an exit cliff. Risk that D'Amaro reverses direction in subsequent quarters and breaks the FY26/FY27 trajectory: bounded by invalidation (i) (margin floor) and (ii) (EPS guide cut). If breach occurs on D'Amaro pivot, mechanical exit fires.

(β) **Technological disruption risk (streaming margin trajectory).** SVOD margin trajectory depends on Disney+ pricing power, ad-tier monetization, and content cost containment vs NFLX/AMZN/AAPL. NFLX is the structural leader at ~30% segment margin; AMZN Prime Video / AAPL TV+ have effectively-unlimited capital backing. Risk: NFLX/AMZN pricing or content-spend pressure forces Disney+ to discount, breaking SVOD margin trajectory. Mitigation: SVOD margin already cleared 10% in Q2 (above FY26 10% guide), demonstrating pricing power post the late-2025 price hikes (per Variety: "results were driven by price hikes implemented in the fall of 2025"). Disney's IP moat (Marvel / Pixar / Lucasfilm / Disney Animation / ESPN direct-to-consumer / Hulu) is differentiated content versus NFLX original library. Subscription-and-affiliate fees +14% YoY in Q2 indicates pricing power reaching realized revenue. Invalidation (i) catches this directly if margin compresses materially.

(γ) **Competitive erosion risk (parks / Experiences segment).** Q2 disclosure: domestic park attendance −1% YoY; global +2%; per-cap spending strong; Core Parks revenue beat guide on broad-based (admissions / F&B / merchandise) outperformance per CFO Johnston Q2 call. Q2 Experiences revenue ~$9.5B (+7% YoY). Macro overhang: gas prices (Iran de-escalation news May 5-6 lowered immediate concern; oil sub-$100 Brent post May 5-6); consumer discretionary pullback risk. CFO Johnston: "we're not immune to the impacts, including how a significant further rise in fuel prices from current levels could eventually lead to changes in consumer behavior" — explicit acknowledgment, NOT outright reset of guide. Risk: macro deterioration → consumer pullback on $1k+ park visits → Experiences segment OI compression. Mitigation: thesis is anchored to STREAMING margin as the primary driver, not parks. Parks are upside optionality but not the trend-metric. A parks-driven EPS miss could trip invalidation (ii) (FY26 EPS guide cut), which is the appropriate response.

(δ) **Concentration risk within D's existing book.** Current D book = RTX (1 position, Industrials / Aerospace & Defense, ~2% of D NAV). DIS would be Communication Services / Entertainment, sector 0% pre-add. Different GICS sector (no sector cap interaction), different cyclical driver (RTX = defense / commercial aerospace / industrial multi-decade backlog conversion vs DIS = consumer discretionary media / streaming margin trajectory / parks pricing power / IP cycle), different beta exposure (RTX beta ~1.0-1.1 industrial profile vs DIS beta 1.41 consumer-media profile). No theme-concentration interaction (no AI-narrative dependency on DIS — DIS streaming margin trajectory is content-economics-driven, not AI-infrastructure-driven). Trailing-252-day daily-return correlation (estimate, classical-method delegation deferred to fill-capture session if material-bound test required): historical RTX-DIS daily-return correlation typically 0.2-0.35, well below the 0.6 entry-time bucket threshold. No correlation-bucket interaction.

(ε) **Regulatory risk (FCC TV-license review on ABC stations).** Recent news (per StockAnalysis news ticker May 5-6): FCC Chair Brendan Carr opened review of Disney TV station license renewals (ABC affiliates). Per WSJ / Reuters / NYP coverage: the review was framed as "about DEI, not Jimmy Kimmel" per Carr; broadcast group flagged "significant uncertainty"; review process is unfolding under Trump administration. Risk: forced license divestiture, structural regulatory penalty, content-licensing constraints. Mitigation: ABC TV stations are a small fraction of Disney enterprise value; Linear TV is in secular decline and the FY26 thesis is anchored to streaming + Experiences, not linear network economics. Even an adverse FCC outcome on TV-station licenses would not directly impair the SVOD-margin trajectory or buyback execution. NOT decisive against the thesis; logged as adversarial weight. **Reconsideration trigger if regulatory outcome deteriorates:** if FCC issues an order materially restricting Disney's TV station ownership AND Disney 8-Ks the development as a material adverse impact to FY26/FY27 EPS, that would constitute a corporate-action-grade event triggering re-evaluation of the thesis; this is a thesis-monitoring item, not a pre-entry blocker.

(ζ) **Sentiment / 2.13/2.19 amplification.** DIS is **NOT an AI-narrative beneficiary**. The April 2026 D-batch had 4-of-8 names with 2.13/2.19 nuclear-renaissance / hyperscaler-AI amplification (CEG, VST, GOOGL, CCJ — all NO-GO). Pre-mortem 2.14 mitigation via 8-quarter input window applies; the thesis structurally requires multi-quarter trend-evidence (Q1 8.4% + Q2 10.6%), not single-quarter recency anchoring. 2.13 ordinal-tier conviction calibration applies (see Conviction calibration section below).

**Adversarial weight summary (closing).** Bull case: clean Q2 print with two-observation trend establishing 8.4% → 10.6% margin trajectory; FY26/FY27 reaffirmation under new CEO debut; buyback raise to $8B; consensus PT $129-133 implies +20-23% upside vs current $108; -13% from 52-wk high $124.69 leaves room without being capitulation territory; Iran de-escalation news removes immediate consumer-spending overhang; SVOD-margin-trajectory thesis is differentiated from AI-narrative-beneficiary cluster. **Criterion 4 — Subtype B invalidation criteria (quantitative thresholds, public-information observable, immutable through position life).**

(i) **Primary invalidation — SVOD margin floor.** Entertainment SVOD operating margin falls below 8% for 2 consecutive quarters. Two-consecutive-quarter framing prevents single-quarter content-spend lumpiness from auto-invalidating; sustained breach below the Q1 FY26 8.4% baseline (-40bps tolerance for measurement noise) trips invalidation. Mechanism-enforced via 8-K segment reporting at quarter-end.

(ii) **Secondary invalidation — FY26 EPS guide cut.** Disney 8-K issues guide cut materially below the FY26 ~12% adj EPS growth ex-53rd-week framing. Materially defined as: revised FY26 adj EPS growth guide ≤6% (i.e., a >6 percentage point cut from current ~12% midpoint). Mechanism-enforced via 8-K guidance reaffirmation/update at quarterly print.

(iii) **Buyback invalidation — pace fall.** FY26 actual buyback execution falls materially below $7B run-rate (i.e., ≤$3B by mid-fiscal-year H1 close per 10-Q cash flow disclosure, ≤$5B at Q3 FY26 print, or 8-K announcement of suspended/reduced buyback program). Mechanism-enforced via 10-Q cash flow disclosure + 8-K capital allocation announcements.

(iv) **Metric-immutability auto-invalidation (rev 30 mechanism).** If Disney restructures segment reporting such that "Entertainment SVOD operating income" or "Entertainment SVOD operating margin" stops being disclosed in its current form for ≥2 consecutive quarters (e.g., rolled into a new aggregate that doesn't permit isolating SVOD economics; redefined to non-comparable metric; eliminated entirely), the thesis auto-invalidates as of the date the second non-conforming quarterly report is released. This is the rev 30 metric-immutability protection against thesis-evading reporting changes.

(v) **Regulatory-impairment escalation (KL #4 boundary case).** FCC issues a final order materially restricting Disney TV-station ownership AND Disney 8-Ks the development as material adverse impact to FY26/FY27 EPS framework. Triggers pre-emptive thesis review (NOT auto-invalidation; reviewed in fresh thesis-construction session). This is the (ε) adversarial-weight item escalation gate.

### Theater-check on this orchestrator review

A 1-of-1 GO disposition on a name that was 5-of-5 NO-GO in the original April D batch warrants explicit theater-check.

First, am I being too aggressive on this re-screen, drifting toward retrospective-correction bias on the original NO-GO? Counter-argument: the original NO-GO was structurally correct given the information available 2026-04-26 (Subtype B premature with one observation, management-execution category framing under KL #4, 10 trading days before D'Amaro's first print as CEO). The session-prompt-defined trigger conditions were specific and information-resolvable; they have all mechanically cleared. The trigger-conditions-met → fresh-thesis-run protocol is itself the discipline that prevents original-NO-GO becoming a permanent bar (that would be the "NO-GO records are barriers" anti-pattern explicitly rejected per Operating_Protocols rule). The fresh thesis is constructed under Subtype B with explicit primary-driver reframing per session-prompt step 4 — not a re-statement of the original failed thesis. The trend-evidence is two-observation in hand (Q1 8.4% → Q2 10.6%), exactly the structural condition the original NO-GO flagged as missing. The reframing from management-execution-quality to financial-metric-traceable is the explicit Subtype B requirement, not a rationalization. None of this reads as drift toward over-correction; it reads as the framework working as designed when the underlying conditions resolve.

Second, is the +7.54% Q2-print pop being treated correctly under criterion 6? Counter-argument: I considered whether to apply the GOOGL 2026-04-26 / 2026-04-30 re-screen pattern of treating post-print rallies as criterion-6 violations. GOOGL's pattern was at-ATH-texture (within 1% of all-time-high closing) with trailing-30 estimated +8-10% pre-Q1-print and +27-30%+ post-Q1-print, in conjunction with maximum 2.13/2.19 amplification (Anthropic-investment conflict + AI-narrative-mega-cap). DIS's pattern is fundamentally different: -13% from 52-wk high (NOT at-ATH), trailing-30 +12% (within threshold both pre- and post-print), zero AI-narrative amplification. The +7.54% pop is the trigger-condition-resolution event itself — clearing required substantive financial information that produced the pop. Treating that single-day pop as a fresh criterion-6 violation would conflate the event-resolution mechanism with the criterion-6 rule it tests against, and would create a degenerate framework where any trigger-condition-met re-screen would auto-fail on the print-day pop. The correct framing is: trailing-30-day INCLUDING the print-day pop is the test, and at +12% it is below the +15% threshold. The pop is not separately disqualifying.

Third, is the KL #4 reframing genuine or rhetorical? Counter-argument: I considered whether the "primary-driver reframing from management-execution-quality to financial-metric-traceable" is a substantive Subtype B reconstruction or a rhetorical re-labeling that leaves the underlying KL #4 risk unchanged. The substantive reconstruction has three load-bearing properties: (a) the invalidation criteria are quantitative thresholds on financial metrics (margin, EPS guide, buyback pace), not on management-quality assessments; (b) the trend-evidence anchoring is two-observation quantitative (Q1 8.4% → Q2 10.6%), not narrative-quality assessment; (c) the metric-immutability rev 30 protection ensures the metric stays disclosed in current form or auto-invalidates. These three properties are what distinguish a Subtype B thesis from a management-execution-quality thesis under Strategy.md rev 28-30. A rhetorical re-labeling without these properties would be the failure mode the prompt is testing against; the actual thesis structure has all three properties. KL #4 residual is acknowledged as a SECONDARY contributor (management quality ultimately manifests in metrics) but the thesis is anchored to metrics, and breach manifests in metrics, and exit fires on metric breach. This is the architectural reframing, not rhetorical.

The orchestrator review converges on GO.

Mechanical eligibility (criterion 1, criterion 5 sector cap, instrument rule) all clear with cushion; the decisive flaw is at criterion 4 information-vs-sentiment test under sub-pattern routing.

### Decisive flaw analysis (criterion 4 dual-framing)

**LONG framing decisive flaws (sub-pattern routing layered-1+3 variant):**

(α) **Sub-pattern 1 fingerprint — cleanest-L1-aggressive-ratification post-event PT-raise-wave.** Per 24/7 Wall St. and Schaeffer's compilations: **15 sell-side firms raised price targets in the 24-hour window post-print** (Tue 5/5):
- BofA Global Research: $20 → $27 (+35%) — Buy maintained, the highest absolute PT
- JPMorgan: $20 → $25 (+25%) — rating maintained
- Citi: $19 → $25 (+32%)
- BMO Capital: $21 → $24 (+14%) (per CNN PT-raise list)
- Piper Sandler: $21 → $26 (+24%)
- Guggenheim: $21 → $24 (+14%)
- Plus ~9 additional firms with PT raises documented in 24/7 Wall St. and Schaeffer's "no fewer than 15 analysts" framings
- Pre-print analyst landscape: 19 Buy / 19 Hold / 1 Sell (TickerNerd; mostly Hold-skewed split decision)
- Post-print consensus PT ~$26.52-$27.89 vs current ~$21 close = +24-32% upside notional
- This is the canonical sub-pattern 1 fingerprint that produced the BE 2026-05-01 / CAT 2026-05-02 / AXSM 2026-05-06 NO-GO disposition. The aggressive PT-raise wave INDICATES that the print is genuinely new information (real Q1 beat + Q2 guide above consensus + adj EBITDA beat), and the sell-side has now moved consensus PT levels to reflect that information. **The implication for B is decisive: aggressive PT-raises = information-driven repricing. The market reaction (+6.83% close-to-close) is part of, not an overshoot of, that information-driven repricing.**

(β) **Sub-pattern 3 fingerprint — information-priced-via-pre-print-rally.** Per Motley Fool: "Shares have soared about 25% from early April" pre-print. PINS rallied from ~$17.50 in early April to $20.86 on May 4 close = **+19.2% pre-print rally** absorbing the AI-driven ad turnaround narrative. Per Motley Fool: "In early April, I argued that shares of Pinterest looked oversold." The bull narrative (AI-driven ad targeting + monetization-finally-outrunning-audience-growth + tvScientific CTV optionality + activist Elliott $1B stake + $2B buyback) was already in market consciousness and had already moved the stock +19% pre-print. The +6.83% post-event close-to-close is the SECOND repricing leg on top of the +19% pre-print absorption. **The forward narrative was substantially priced in BEFORE the print**, leaving smaller residual edge for B's post-event mean-reversion mechanism. This is the same fingerprint that produced the AXSM 2026-05-04 NO-GO (FDA approval + Q1 print event with pre-print PT-cluster mean $226 absorbed forward narrative).

(γ) **NEW evidence layer — "move-completely-faded-by-Day-2" sub-evidence.** The post-event price trajectory shows the move FADED rapidly:
- Mon 5/4 close (pre-print): $20.86
- Mon 5/4 AH +18.94% to $24.81 (Benzinga)
- Tue 5/5 pre-market: as much as +19% from Mon close (~$24.80)
- Tue 5/5 close (event-day close): $22.28 (+6.83% from Mon close, but already -10.2% from Mon AH peak)
- Wed 5/6 day range: high $22.35, low $20.70, close ~$21.13 (-5.16% from Tue close)
- Thu 5/7 (today, this session): "trading marginally lower on Thursday" per StockAnalysis news — likely $20.85-21.10 area, near pre-print baseline
- **Post-event move trajectory: from +18.94% AH peak Mon → +6.83% Tue close → ~+1.3% Wed close → ~+0% Thu (this session)** = approximately 80%+ retrace of post-event rally within 2 trading days. The mean reversion that B's mechanism is built to capture has already SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLETED. There is no remaining post-event mispricing to exploit at the level of the Tuesday peak or the Tuesday close.
- Per Motley Fool May 5: "the enthusiasm for the results notably faded as the stock was up as much as 19% in pre-market trading before closing up just 7%" — this fade-from-peak pattern was observable from Day 1 itself, and Wednesday's continuation of the fade confirms the market has decisively priced the print's information. **The market itself has rendered the verdict that the +18.94% AH pop was sentiment-driven overshoot that overstated the information content; the close-to-close +6.83% was the partial repricing toward equilibrium; and Wed/Thu's continuation back near pre-print baseline ($20.86) is the equilibrium settling.**
- This is a NEW evidence layer not previously seen in the sub-pattern 1 instance string (BE/CAT/AXSM all had stocks holding closer to event-day-close levels through Day 2-5 of the post-event window). PINS is the cleanest case yet of "sell-side aggressive PT-raise + market-pricing-down-the-PT-raise within 2 trading days" — the divergence between sell-side ratification (consensus PT $26.52) and market reaction (~$21) is itself the criterion-4 information-vs-sentiment evidence: the market is voting that the aggressive PT raises are NOT going to validate at near-term mean-reversion horizon.

(δ) **Quality-of-revenue concern.** Q1 ad metrics: ad impressions +24% YoY (volume), ad pricing **−5% YoY** (decline). Revenue growth +18% is volume-driven, not pricing-driven. ARPU global +6% / UCAN +9% / Europe +17% / Rest of World +38% — the volume scaling is real but the price-per-ad decline indicates either advertiser-budget pressure, lower-CPM ad mix, or platform pricing-power weakness. Per Motley Fool May 5 second article: "Pinterest's ad pricing fell 5% year over year, with all of the revenue growth coming from a 24% jump in ad impressions." Plus: tvScientific CTV acquisition adds ~100bps margin drag in 2026 per management commentary; CEO Ready: "AI-powered ads platform that delivers performance for advertisers" framing argues volume-growth-via-AI, but the price-per-ad decline is the structural concern. The bull thesis depends on 2026-2027 AI-driven targeting improvements lifting ARPU; that trajectory is multi-quarter and not resolvable within B's 60-day mean-reversion horizon. **This is a fundamental-quality concern that cuts against B's mispricing thesis: the +6.83% close-to-close already prices the print's volume-strength positively, but the price-per-ad weakness leaves residual fundamental concern that consensus PT $26-$28 may not validate even on a 12-month horizon.**

(ε) **Convergence target structural failure under criterion 3 closed-list rev 14.** Strategy.md criterion 3 admits two convergence-target types: (a) numerical price level OR (b) specific event from strict-enumerated closed list (next earnings release / next FDA decision date / next FOMC meeting / S&P 500-Russell 1000-Nasdaq 100 inclusion announcement).
- (a) Numerical target chase: chasing the post-print sell-side consensus PT cluster ($26.52-$27.89) is **the canonical sub-pattern 1 trap** — the doctrine established by BE/CAT/STX/MDLZ/AXSM is that aggressive PT-raise consensus levels post-event should NOT be used as B convergence targets, because the targets reflect information-driven repricing the sell-side has already executed and the stock has already partially absorbed. A 25% gap-fill from current ~$21 toward the sell-side $27 cluster would target ~$22.50; a 50% gap-fill would target ~$24. Both are within day-trading noise of recent levels. The numerical-target framing fails because the "gap" the convergence target is meant to close has already been substantially closed by post-event price action (Tue close $22.28) and then re-opened in the wrong direction (Wed close $21.13).
- (b) Event-based target: PINS next earnings release scheduled Aug 4-6 2026 per CNBC/TradingView (reported as both Aug 4 and Aug 6) — falls **outside** 60-day window from May 4 entry (60 days = July 3, 2026). Window boundary fails this option. No FDA event applicable. No FOMC mismatch (PINS not FOMC-correlated event). No imminent index-inclusion catalyst (PINS already in S&P MidCap 400; no S&P 500 inclusion announcement imminent per public disclosure).
- **No admissible convergence target exists under criterion 3 closed-list rev 14 for the LONG framing.** This is a structural failure of criterion 3, distinct from but compounding the criterion 4 sub-pattern routing decisive flaw.

(ζ) **Pre-mortem 2.4 narrative over-fit residual + Constraint 1 partial-mitigation framing.** Per Strategy.md pre-mortem rev 7 Constraint 1: "By self-reference, no in-distribution discriminator exists outside the biased judgment" on whether a market reaction "looks overdone." The PINS bull thesis would frame the +6.83% close-to-close (or the now-faded post-event price near pre-print baseline) as "underdone given Q2 guide raise + AI-driven monetization acceleration." But the Tuesday close $22.28 → Wednesday close $21.13 → Thursday near $20.85-21.10 trajectory IS the market's discriminator, and it is voting AGAINST the underdone framing. Self-reference closure: the LONG framing's plausibility depends on assuming the market is wrong (in a sentiment-overshoot direction), but the market's continued repricing-away from the post-print euphoria is itself informative evidence the market is correct. ~70% structural residual on 2.4 (per pre-mortem KL #2) is the empirical baseline; on this PINS setup the residual binds.

**SHORT framing decisive flaws:**

(η) **Mean reversion already substantially complete.** Entering a SHORT at current ~$21 against a stock that has already retraced from $22.28 Tue close to ~$21 Wed/Thu close leaves negligible remaining mean-reversion edge. The "overshoot" the SHORT thesis would target has already played out — the stock is back near pre-print baseline ($20.86). Short-thesis convergence target would need to be below $20.86 (i.e., post-rally MEAN reversion BELOW pre-print baseline), which requires an entirely different thesis: not "post-event overshoot mean-reverts to baseline" but "post-event overshoot mean-reverts BELOW baseline because the print itself was structurally bearish." That thesis is decisively flawed because Q1 was a beat-and-raise — the print was substantively positive at the headline level (revenue beat, EPS beat, EBITDA beat, MAU beat, Q2 guide raise).

(θ) **Shorting against (a) Q1 beat + Q2 guide raise (real new information), (b) 15 aggressive PT raises (canonical sub-pattern 1 mirror against short), (c) pre-print rally already happened, (d) high short interest 15.4% of float (structural squeeze risk per Strategy B KL #7 short-side gap-up execution residual).** All four directional-tape factors run against a B short. Pre-print short interest at 15.4% of float (per 24/7 Wall St. citing Feb 2026 data: "Short interest in Pinterest has surged 123.5%, with 15.4% of the float now sold short ahead of earnings") is structural squeeze fuel. The Mon AH +18.94% pop was likely partially driven by short-cover dynamics; entering NEW short here would re-expose to that same dynamic if any further bullish catalyst (e.g., follow-on PT raises, JPMorgan TMT mid-May or BofA Tech early-June conference commentary, intra-quarter ad-revenue commentary) arrives within the 60-day window.

(ι) **Strategy.md short-side stop-loss at +25% from short-entry binds on squeeze.** Short entry near $21 → +25% trigger at $26.25 — within the BofA $27 PT level + within plausible squeeze toward consensus $26.52 PT. Per pre-mortem KL #7 (rev 4 rewritten): in gap-up conditions, the stop is operational not structural — execution prices can be substantially above +25%, leaving realized loss uncapped. PINS is exactly the gap-up-prone setup KL #7 names: high short interest, post-print sell-side ratification, narrative-momentum stock with retail Reddit-flip-bullish (per 24/7 Wall St.: "Reddit sentiment ... swinging from very bearish (18) on May 1 to bullish (78) by May 5"), low absolute share price (~$21) where small dollar moves = large percentage moves.

(κ) **Pre-mortem Constraint 2 — 2.20 textbook-rational-penalty trap is canonical.** B's mechanism IS the textbook-rational instinct (that prices return to fundamental value). Shorting against a beat-and-raise post-Q1 with bull-ratification IS exactly the strategy mechanism's structural exposure point. Per pre-mortem rev 7: "B is structurally exposed to 2.20 because the strategy's mechanism is precisely the textbook-rational instinct applied after an overreaction. The router's HIGH-VIX exclusion is a partial regime-level mitigation; no mechanism-level mitigation exists." Current regime is risk-on (SPY ATH 7,365.12 per Daily.md 2026-05-06; Russell record; XLK +2.2% / XLI +2.7% Wed; Iran de-escalation news; broad market rally) — exactly the regime in which short-against-bull-ratification 2.20-traps fire. The 6+ consecutive NO-GO B-short precedent string in current regime (BE 2026-05-01 / CAT 2026-05-02 / TWLO 2026-05-02 / UPS 2026-05-05 / NCLH 2026-05-05 / CRCL 2026-05-05 / SHOP 2026-05-06 D2-declined / PYPL 2026-05-06 D2-declined / CDW 2026-05-06 D2-declined) demonstrates this 2.20-trap is binding empirically; PINS-short would extend the string to 10 consecutive NO-GO B-shorts in this regime.

(λ) **SHORT framing convergence target structurally fails too.** Numerical target below $20.86 (pre-print baseline): even targeting -10% from short-entry $21 = $18.90 requires the thesis "Q1 beat-and-raise prints are structurally bearish on PINS" which is incompatible with the Q2 guide raise + adj EBITDA beat reality. Event-based target: same window-boundary failure as LONG framing on next earnings Aug 4-6. **No admissible convergence target for SHORT either.**

### Adversarial counter-argument (engaging with the "is this really a NO-GO?" question)

(μ) **Counter:** "Q2 guide raise is genuinely above consensus by 2-4%; the market reaction is moderate (+6.83% close-to-close, not blowout); pre-print rally was driven by oversold-bounce not narrative-anticipation; sell-side PT raises reflect actual financial improvement; entering long here at near-pre-print baseline ($20.85-21.10) provides clean entry below sell-side consensus and at fundamentally improved underlying business." Counter-counter: this argument essentially restates the bull thesis without engaging with the move-completely-faded-by-Day-2 evidence. The market voted the moderate +6.83% close-to-close was already overstated; the Wed/Thu retrace toward pre-print baseline is the market completing the information-pricing exercise. Entering LONG at ~$21 today is entering AT the market's revised equilibrium — there's no mispricing remaining for B to capture. Plus the sub-pattern 1 PT-raise-wave is the canonical bull-trap fingerprint that has produced 4 prior NO-GO dispositions; sample size is small but pattern convergence is consistent.

(ν) **Counter:** "PINS at $21 vs consensus PT $26.52 = +26% upside; that's the post-event mispricing B is built to identify." Counter-counter: the consensus PT post-print reflects 15 firms moving up their targets in 24h post-print; this is INFORMATION pricing, not sentiment overshoot. Per BE/CAT/STX/MDLZ doctrine, chasing post-event-aggressive-PT-cluster as a B convergence target is the canonical sub-pattern 1 trap. The PT-cluster represents the sell-side's revised valuation framework given Q1 print + Q2 guide; it's not a residual mispricing the market hasn't caught. The market's revealed preference (Wed/Thu trading near pre-print baseline) is the market's pricing-disagreement with the aggressive PT raises — the market is voting that ad-pricing -5% YoY and tvScientific CTV margin drag and the irreducible LTV/CAC tradeoffs in social-discovery monetization will compress the multi-quarter trajectory below the sell-side PT cluster expectations.

(ξ) **Counter:** "B has a 25-NO-GO / 3-GO track record; aren't you over-rejecting?" Counter-counter: per Operating_Protocols "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" rule, prior NO-GOs do not gate fresh evaluation. Each NO-GO this session is judged on its own per-name decisive-flaw analysis. PINS is an independent evaluation. The 4-instance sub-pattern 1 string + 9-instance B-short NO-GO string in current regime are CONVERGENT framework signals, not over-rejection bias — the framework is empirically calibrated to reject this exact pattern, and the convergence pattern affirms calibration is working. Furthermore, the current session's earlier disposition was a GO (DIS Strategy D); GO outcomes happen when the trigger conditions / pattern fingerprint resolve toward entry. PINS does not. The orchestrator review converges on NO-GO.

### Decisive flaw analysis (criterion 4 dual-framing)

**LONG framing decisive flaws:**

(α) **Information content of the print is MODEST and rally magnitude exceeds.** Print components and information value:
- Q1 FFO-as-Adj $0.45 vs $0.43 cons = +$0.02 / +4.7% beat (NORMAL-sized REIT beat magnitude, not blowout)

- Janus Living IPO completed March 2026; $880M proceeds; Healthpeak retains 81.6%. **This is ALREADY-PUBLIC information from March 2026, not new at Q1 print time.**

- Lab leasing improvement + Outpatient Medical strong = real fundamental info but multi-quarter trajectory.
- Net debt to EBITDA 5.4x = stable balance sheet, not deleveraging step-change.

(β) **Rally drivers are dominantly SENTIMENT-side per primary Investing.com framing.** Per Investing.com explicit list: "The combination of (i) a massive earnings surprise, (ii) an upward revision to full-year FFO guidance, (iii) a supportive earnings call on the morning of May 6, (iv) a strengthened balance sheet following the Janus Living IPO and new term loan, (v) positive peer results from Welltower and Ventas, and (vi) a risk-on broader market environment all converged to push DOC sharply higher." ### Why criterion 1 is the binding constraint (parallel to AXSM 2026-05-02 + EQIX 2026-05-01 precedents)

Across all four plausible event-day reference windows, the actual close-to-close measurements yield +2.01% / +1.10% / +3.13% / -1.33% — all materially below the 5% threshold by 37-100% relative shortfall.

### Decision

**SMCI — NO-GO (DECLINE).** Criterion 4 dual-framing decisive failure with **sub-pattern 4 variant 4d "active-securities-litigation-overhang" FIRST INSTANCE established** per D2 5/6 routing pre-reservation. The +24.54% Day-0 close-to-close pop on Wed 5/6 is information-driven repricing on real Q3 EPS BEAT ($0.84 vs $0.61 cons +37.7%) + FY26 guide raised to ≥$40B + CEO Charles Liang validating AI-server-demand durability — BUT this information-positive print does NOT resolve or materially reduce the multi-vector structural overhang stack priced into SMCI for 6-18+ months with multi-year resolution timeline structurally outside Strategy B's 60-day mean-reversion window. **6-vector structural overhang factor stack:**
1. **Active securities class action** — Bhuva v. Super Micro Computer, Inc., No. 26-cv-02606 (N.D. Cal.) + City of Hialeah Employees Retirement System v. Super Micro Computer, Inc., et al., No. 26-cv-3018 (N.D. Cal.); **lead-plaintiff application deadline May 26, 2026** (15 calendar days from today)
2. **Underlying federal criminal indictment** of 3 individuals for "scheme to divert massive quantities of servers housing U.S. artificial intelligence technology to customers in China" violating U.S. export control laws
3. **Class period 2024-04-30 through 2026-03-19** = ~23 months damages exposure
4. **Hindenburg Research short-seller report August 2024** — extensive allegations (accounting irregularities + related-party transactions + recidivist-violator pattern from prior 2018-2020 SEC enforcement + export-control violations + governance concerns) priced 18+ months
